key_insight: PEARL combines reinforcement learning with differentiable physics and adjoint sensitivities to make real-time optimal control more sample-efficient and scalable for high-dimensional dynamical systems.
engineering_relevance: This approach can reduce simulation cost and improve deployability for control of complex engineering systems such as flow navigation, robotics, and other parametric dynamical processes.
method: Uses an actor-adjoint algorithm to compute policy gradients over short horizons.
Leverages automatic differentiation and adjoint-based sensitivities of future returns approximated by neural networks.
Exploits differentiable dynamics to guide policy learning and reduce environment interactions.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on two challenging parametric navigation problems in unsteady flows, where it outperforms state-of-the-art RL, generalizes across scenarios, and scales to high-dimensional state/action spaces.
watch_item: Performance depends on access to differentiable environment models and accurate adjoint/NN approximations, which may limit use when the physics model is noisy or only partially known.
paper_title: Physics-enhanced reinforcement learning for real-time optimal control of dynamical systems
